source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1090 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1090 was established by Ordinance No. 32272, passed by the Dallas City Council on August 24, 2022. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1090 is established on property generally located southwest of Cleveland Street between Park Row Avenue and South Boulevard. The size of PD 1090 is approximately 1.23 acres. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article, BLANK WALL AREA means any portion of the exterior of a building that does not include a material change, windows, doors, columns, pilasters, or other articulation greater than 12 inches in depth. Blank wall area is measured horizontally on each story.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district.

(d) The primary street in this district is Cleveland Street. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 1090A: development plan. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a convalescent and nursing home, hospice care, and related institutions use and office use, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 1090A) and Section 51A-13.703 does not apply. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) The building shown on the development plan is a mixed-use shopfront development type as defined in Section 51A-13.304(b).

(c) For all other uses, a site plan must be approved in accordance with Section 51A- 13.703. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the WMU-3 Walkable Urban Mixed Use District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the WMU-3 Walkable Urban Mixed Use District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the WMU-3 Walkable Urban Mixed Use District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review
(DIR) in the WMU-3 Walkable Urban Mixed Use District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following use is permitted by right:

-- Convalescent and nursing home, hospice care, and related institutions. [limited to a maximum of 80 beds] (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls).

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the WMU-3 Walkable Urban Mixed Use District apply.

(b) Convalescent and nursing home, hospice care, and related institution use and office use. The following yard, lot, and space regulations apply:

(1) Building setbacks.

(A) Cleveland Street.

(i) Minimum building setback is 10 feet.

(ii) Maximum building setback is 30 feet.

(B) South Boulevard.

(i) Minimum building setback is 10 feet.

(ii) Maximum building setback is 25 feet.

(C) Park Row Avenue.

(i) Minimum building setback is 10 feet.

(ii) No maximum building setback.

(B) Service street/alley.

(i) Minimum building setback is five feet.

(ii) No maximum building setback.

(2) Parking setbacks.

(A) Cleveland Street and Park Row Avenue. Minimum parking setback is five feet.

(B) South Boulevard. Minimum parking setback is 30 feet.

(B) Service street/alley. Minimum parking setback is five feet.

(3) Floor area. Maximum floor area is 50,000 square feet.

(4) Height. Maximum structure height is 60 feet.

(5) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 40 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(6) Stories.

(A) Maximum number of stories above grade is four.

(B) Ground story.

(i) Minimum story height is 15 feet.

(ii) Maximum story height is 30 feet.

(C) Upper story.

(i) Minimum story height is 10 feet.

(ii) Maximum story height is 15 feet. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A- 13.400 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) For a convalescent and nursing home, hospice care, and related institutions use and office use, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(c) Surface parking may only be located in the area shown on the development plan.

(d) Surface parking adjacent to a street must be screened from the street using one or more of the following materials:

(1) A three-foot high earthen berm planted with turf grass or ground cover recommended for local use by the building official. The berm may not have a slope that exceeds one-foot of height for each three-feet of width.

(2) A minimum three-foot high solid masonry wall.

(3) Hedge-like evergreen plant materials recommended for local use by the building official. The plant materials must be located in a bed that is at least three-feet wide with a minimum soil depth of 24 inches. Initial plantings must be capable of obtaining a solid appearance within three years. Plant materials must be placed 36 inches on center over the entire length of the bed unless a landscape architect recommends an alternative planting density that the building official determines is capable of providing a solid appearance within three years. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Landscaping And Pedestrian Amenities
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.111. LANDSCAPING AND PEDESTRIAN AMENITIES.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Section 51A-13.304.

(b) For a convalescent and nursing home, hospice care, and related institutions use and office use, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(c) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(d) One bench, trash receptacle, or bike rack must be provided per every 75 linear feet in the pedestrian zones as shown on the development plan.

(e) Pedestrian lighting must be provided in accordance with Section 51A-13.601. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Fences
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.112. FENCES.

(a) A fence may be located on the perimeter of the Property in the area shown on the development plan.

(b) Fences may be a maximum six feet in height and may consist of decorative architectural metal or wrought iron so long as they are open such that no more than 25 percent of the surface area of the fence obstructs a view through the fence from a position perpendicular to the fence. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Design Standards For Convalescent And
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.113. DESIGN STANDARDS FOR CONVALESCENT AND NURSING HOME, HOSPICE CARE, AND RELATED INSTITUTIONS USE.

(a) Ground-story transparency. The following minimum transparency is required for street-facing facades: (Measured between 0 and 10 ft above adjacent sidewalk.)

(1) Cleveland Street. Minimum 25 percent.

(2) South Boulevard. Minimum 40 percent.

(3) Park Row Avenue. None.

(b) Upper-story transparency. The following minimum transparency is required for street facing facades:

(1) Cleveland Street. Minimum 10 percent.

(2) South Boulevard. Minimum 20 percent.

(3) Park Row Avenue and service street/alley. None.

(c) Blank wall area. Maximum blank wall area is 20 linear feet along Cleveland Street.

(d) Street frontage. The following minimum street frontage is required:

(1) Cleveland Street. Minimum 40 percent.

(2) South Boulevard. Minimum 70 percent.

(3) Park Row Avenue and service street/alley. None. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Streetscapes
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.114. STREETSCAPES.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult Division 51A-13.500 for streetscape requirements.

(b) For a convalescent and nursing home, hospice care, and related institutions use and office use, streetscapes must be provided as shown on the development plan. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.115. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for WMU zoning districts in Section 51A-13.603. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32272)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1090.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance

with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32272)
